content_blocks.title: Practice reasoning
content_blocks.text: A pipeline binds the preprocessing and estimator steps together so the same ordered workflow is used for training and prediction. For feature selection in pipelines, keep the problem definition, data selection, estimator configuration, and evaluation criterion explicit. When results are uncertain, compare a baseline and inspect examples rather than treating one metric as a complete explanation.

content_blocks.code:
from sklearn.pipeline import make_pipeline
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression
from sklearn.datasets import load_iris
X, y = load_iris(return_X_y=True)
model = make_pipeline(StandardScaler(), LogisticRegression(max_iter=1000, random_state=0))
model.fit(X, y)
print(model.predict(X[:2]).tolist())

content_blocks.title: Common mistakes and fixes
content_blocks.text: Check input shapes, target alignment, data types, missing values, label order, and whether the expected output assumes a fixed random seed. Fit learned preprocessing only on training data, preferably inside a Pipeline. Do not select parameters by repeatedly looking at the final test set.
